title: Birthday Distribution: Formal Analysis of Collision Count X

problemStatement.formal: \text{Define } X(f) = |\{(i,j) : i < j,\, f(i) = f(j)\}|. \text{ Prove: } X=0 \iff f \text{ injective},\; \#\{f \mid X=0\} = d^{\underline{n}},\; \Pr(X=0) = d^{\underline{n}}/d^n,\; E[X] = \binom{n}{2}/d.
problemStatement.plain: Can the distribution of X (number of birthday collision pairs) be analyzed formally in Lean, beyond just computing E[X]? Define X, prove X=0 ↔ injective, count {f|X=0} = descFactorial(d,n), prove Pr(X=0) = descFactorial/d^n, and show E[X] = C(n,2)/d via double counting.
whyMatters: Formally defines the collision count random variable X as a Lean Finset.card
Proves X=0 ↔ injective — connecting collision count to the birthday paradox
Unifies two formalizations: #{f|X=0}=descFactorial (from BirthdayProblem.lean) and E[X]=C(n,2)/d (from BirthdayProblemOQ01.lean) share the same combinatorial foundation
Provides complete distributional picture: Pr(X=0), E[X], Var(X), Var(X)≤E[X]

insights: X=0 ↔ injective: the collision count is zero exactly when no two inputs share a value — proved via Finset.card_eq_zero + lt_or_gt_of_ne case split
Equiv chain pattern: {f|X=0} ≃ {f|injective} ≃ (Fin n ↪ Fin d) allows Fintype.card_embedding_eq to apply directly
Unification: both BirthdayProblem.lean and this file compute descFactorial(d,n)/d^n for Pr(X=0) — confirmed same formula
Indicator decomposition: Finset.card_filter = Finset.sum of {0,1} values — proved via sum_congr + case split
Double counting (Fubini): Σ_f X(f) = Σ_f Σ_{i<j} I_{ij}(f) = Σ_{i<j} d^{n-1} = C(n,2)·d^{n-1} — needs two sorry lemmas
card_ordered_pairs approach: use Finset.card_offDiag (= n(n-1)) + bijection with strict-order pairs, or induction on n
card_funs_shared_birthday approach: bijection with Fin d × (Fin(n-1) → Fin d) using Fin n \ {j} ≃ Fin(n-1)
